profile.beat: Corporate insider purchases and sales (Form 4 style alerts) across all sectors, plus an occasional relayed earnings headline.
profile.style: Templated one-line alerts naming the insider, the company and the transaction, often framed as 'buying the dip', 'buying the rip', 'joins the selling' or a cluster count. The framing highlights unusual size, first-ever trades, reversals and trades against recent price action, but the author never states a personal position or a directional view of their own.
profile.cadence: Roughly hourly alerts during market hours on each trading day of the window, almost all original posts with a chart link; one relayed earnings quote post and one casual reply.
profile.revisits: Follows repeat insider activity on the same names: Borr Drilling buying on consecutive days (2102065856326820006, 2102442076935758104), repeated purchases by Ryan Cohen at GameStop (2102382958787055994) and continued selling at Dell, CrowdStrike and Medpace. These updates report third-party trades, not revisions of the author's own calls.
profile.caveats: Every post relays third-party insider transactions; they are not the author's stance and must not be read as author-conviction picks. Transaction codes, 10b5-1 plans and underlying filings are not established by these texts. The one reply (2102746261250314409) concedes the author had not checked the news before a prior post.

narrative: Over the window the account ran its usual stream of insider-transaction alerts. Buying alerts clustered in beaten-down or small-cap names (Borr Drilling, Fluence Energy, Skillsoft, Centuri, Tennant, AIAI, RTB Digital, Infinity Natural Resources) and in a few names bought after run-ups (Science Applications International, Village Farms, Cybin). A director's largest-ever purchase at Salesforce and further Ryan Cohen buying at GameStop were the most prominent large-cap buys. Selling alerts concentrated on names after strong runs or near highs, notably Scorpio Tankers, Dell, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Dorian LPG and Credo, plus selling into weakness at ServiceTitan and Smartbird. The author frames these as signals worth noticing but never commits to a trade, so no view changed and no author-owned directional picks are extracted.
